messages:
olivia: Heads-up — FinApp (large customer) just asked to lock a latency SLA into the PRD: 95th <= 150ms for hosted text-gen at launch (Q3). Product wants this in scope. This feels tight given our current stacks. any quick thoughts?

sam: Do we have the workload profile? seq lengths / typical tokens / concurrency?

olivia: They said chat-heavy: avg output ~120 tokens, input ~32. Burst patterns around market open (up to 10x baseline for ~3m windows). They also asked for a 99th <= 250ms as an aspirational number.

mike: 150ms @95 is unlikely on hosted for that workload without either smaller models or reserved capacity. Our measured 95th for similar prompts is ~320ms on shared pools. Options: (1) dedicated GPU pool (reserved), (2) smaller model / quantization (quality hit), (3) relax SLA.

jessica: Product priority is "predictable latency" rather than squeezing every last ms. Could we accept a pragmatic set of ACs that trade a slightly higher 95th (200ms) but with strict canary + fallback policies? That buys us time to optimize.

sam: Suggest we frame a decision matrix in PRD: A) Premium SLA (150ms) -> requires dedicated commit / infra cost; B) Hosted SLA (200ms) -> needs caching + q4 quant + routing; C) Not feasible. Attach cost delta for A vs B.

olivia: Draft ACs (for PRD) — please react / edit:

```
Acceptance Criteria:
- 95th latency <= 200ms on canonical launch prompt set at expected burst profile
- 99th latency <= 350ms
- Error budget: <= 1% combined 5xx/timeouts per 24h window
- Quality regression: <= 2% drop on semantic-sim eval vs baseline model
- Canary rollout: 2% traffic for 48h, observe SLOs, then stepwise ramp
- Automatic fallback: on sustained SLO burn > 30m, route to smaller model variant with quality guardrails
```

mike: Those ACs seem like a fair compromise. Engineering note: hitting 200ms 95th will require prefix/KV caching + adaptive batching heuristics + q4 quantization on the chosen model. I can validate with perf sims. Need to surface the expected GPU delta for the dedicated path.

deploy-bot: Reminder: create RFC + link PRD before next sync. See template: /docs/rfcs/0000-model-sla-template.md

jessica: Product decision proposal: present the two commercial options to Sales — Hosted SLA at 200ms (default) + optional Dedicated (150ms) with a commit. That keeps us honest and avoids overpromising. Also include acceptance criteria and fallback behavior.

sam: Action items: Mike -> run perf sim (canonical prompts + burst profile) by EOD Wed; Olivia -> update PRD with ACs + commercial options; Jessica -> draft customer-facing reply with provisional numbers and tradeoffs. Ops: prepare runbook snippet for the fallback route.

olivia: Thanks — I'll update the PRD now and tag eng for perf numbers. TL;DR: don't promise 150ms on hosted unless we take dedicated commitment.

ops-bot: NOTE: Add SLO alerting thresholds to the PRD (p95 warn at 70% of target, p95 critical at 100% of target).
